heldout_scope.definition: Held out from the current route-146/148/203 mechanism-development pilot.
heldout_scope.warning: This manifest does not establish exclusion from ORION pretraining or adapter training data. Make a separate dataset-lineage check before using the phrase training-held-out.

selection_rules.current_environment_gate: Each route still requires one clean_off replay in the current environment before any corrupt condition is run.

spatial_corruption_pairing_policy.event_window: Calibrate the first hazard-visible and conflict-resolved frames from a clean trace, then freeze the same route-progress window for every condition.
spatial_corruption_pairing_policy.on_path_region: A compact region intersecting the projected ego path corridor and the relevant pedestrian, cyclist, or vehicle conflict region.
spatial_corruption_pairing_policy.off_path_region: A same-view, equal-area region with matched baseline luminance that does not intersect the projected path corridor or relevant actor.
matching_constraints: same seed when the corruption is stochastic
spatial_corruption_pairing_policy.important_note: The XML trigger point anchors scenario activation; it is not automatically the first frame in which the hazard is visible or safety-critical.

candidates.why_suitable: Closest held-out transfer check for route 146: the same cyclist/pedestrian crossing mechanism occurs in Town02, with a blocker that makes a compact path-intersecting corruption causally plausible. A matched off-path patch tests whether location, rather than corruption energy alone, matters.

A pedestrian emerges from a parking-side context into the future corridor. The actor/conflict area is compact and spatially separable from an equal-area off-path patch, so it directly probes whether localized uncertainty changes yielding or braking.

A moving vehicle crosses the ego conflict zone against the signal. Corrupting the approaching vehicle or conflict-zone patch should be more safety-relevant than an equally sized non-conflict patch, while the clean reference shows ORION can complete the route without intervention.

A parked vehicle cuts into the ego lane, creating a localized moving hazard whose image support transitions from roadside to future path. That transition is useful for an on-path/off-path spatial counterfactual and for checking response timing.

Three moving bicycles encroach from the side lane ahead. Their lateral relation to the future path changes over time, making this a useful localization-and-timing test rather than a global anomaly test.

A faster Town05 variant of the side-lane bicycle hazard. The higher configured ego speed raises the chance that a short, localized visual degradation creates a measurable safety margin change without requiring full-view dropout.

Adds oncoming traffic to the bicycle encroachment and therefore stresses whether local uncertainty is tied to the actual future-path hazard. It is reserve-tier because the opposite flow adds a control confound absent from routes 164 and 168.

The ego must turn left across an unsignalized actor flow. The conflict-zone portion of the front view is naturally separable from a non-conflict region, but continuous traffic makes this harder to attribute than a single crossing actor, so it remains reserve-tier.
